cards.title: Everything that happened, in order
cards.text: 42 on-track passes, 2 pit stops, 0 cars that never finished.

cards.title: 52 places changed hands before the first lap was done
cards.text: Twenty cars funnelling into the first corner on cold tyres and full tanks. Russell, Gasly and Colapinto came out of it best, and none of them had to pass anybody cleanly to do it: on lap 1 the places are simply there for whoever is brave into the first braking zone. Most of this is the pack sorting itself out. Some of it decides the afternoon.

cards.title: 16 overtakes on this lap alone
cards.text: Bottas, Albon and Verstappen all found a way through on the same lap, which almost never happens by coincidence. Cold tyres, full tanks and everybody still finding out where they belong. 10 different drivers gained a place here.

cards.title: Albon starts P22. Where does he finish?
cards.text: He is in a car that belongs further up the road than this, and he has the whole afternoon to prove it.
cards.reveal: P22 to P18, 4 places, and almost none of it on television. This is the drive nobody will talk about on Monday.

cards.title: 7 overtakes on this lap alone
cards.text: Bortoleto, Alonso and Hadjar all found a way through on the same lap, which almost never happens by coincidence. Cold tyres, full tanks and everybody still finding out where they belong. 7 different drivers gained a place here.

cards.title: 4 overtakes on this lap alone
cards.text: Leclerc, Piastri and Lawson all found a way through on the same lap, which almost never happens by coincidence. Cold tyres, full tanks and everybody still finding out where they belong. 3 different drivers gained a place here.

cards.title: Leclerc: 4 overtakes
cards.text: More than anybody else out there, in a Ferrari, and he started P4 and finished P5. Passing is the part of this sport that looks like the whole sport on television and turns out to be the rarest thing in it: most positions change in the pit lane, not on the road.

cards.title: Track at 41°C, and falling to 32°C
cards.text: Hot tarmac punishes tyres and rewards whoever is gentlest with them. As it cools, the picture flips. It stayed dry.

cards.title: 4 incidents looked at
cards.text: Turn 3 Incident Involving Cars 11 (Per) And 14 (Alo) Noted - Causing A Collision (12:05:54). Being noted is not the same as being punished: most of these are looked at, argued over on the radio, and quietly dropped a few laps later.

cards.title: Lap 6: contact between Perez and Alonso at Turn 3. What do you give?
cards.text: Race control has flagged it and the whole thing lands on your desk while the cars keep circulating. Same call the stewards had to make, same three seconds to think about it.

outcomes.none: You let it go. Nobody loses a place at a desk, and the driver behind spends the rest of the afternoon on the radio.
outcomes.5: Five seconds gets added at the next stop, or to the final time if they never stop again. Usually one position, sometimes none.
outcomes.10: Ten seconds is a real punishment and it almost always costs track position, which is why teams argue so hard about it.

cards.reveal: The stewards went with 10s penalty. Perez served it and still finished P22.

cards.title: Antonelli takes the lead from Hamilton
cards.text: The lead changed hands 3 times on track today, which is rarer than it sounds.

cards.title: 9 lap times deleted
cards.text: The white line is the track. Put a wheel beyond it and the lap simply stops counting, however quick it was. Stroll lost 3 of them, more than anybody, which is the sort of thing that turns into a penalty if it keeps happening. It sounds pedantic until you remember the alternative is letting everybody find their own edge of the circuit.

cards.title: Hadjar hit 340 km/h
cards.text: Top speed says as much about wing level and about sitting in somebody's tow as it does about the engine, which is why the quickest car through the trap is so rarely the quickest car over a lap. Hadjar was running a Red Bull Racing that clearly gave something up in the corners to get it.

cards.title: 2 stops, and the busiest lap saw 1 of them
cards.text: Once one car blinks the rest have to answer. The window opened around here and the busiest single lap was 2, with 1 cars in on the same tour. The quickest trip belonged to Stroll at 30.9s, and the slowest to Perez at 48.6s. That gap is a whole position, sometimes two, decided by people who never touch the steering wheel.

cards.title: 1 penalty calls
cards.text: Perez 10s for causing a collision. A time penalty is served at the next stop, or added to the final time when there is no stop left to serve it at, which is how a result gets rewritten twenty minutes after the flag.

cards.kicker: Your call on the pit wall
cards.title: You are Hamilton, 1.0s behind Antonelli and going nowhere. Now what?
cards.text: Stuck in dirty air your tyres cook and your car will not turn. Stopping first gives you clean track for two or three laps, which is the whole trick behind the undercut.

choices.label: Box now and undercut
choices.sub: Fresh tyres, clean air, two laps to make it pay

choices.label: Stay out and overcut
choices.sub: Let him stop first, then push on an empty track

choices.label: Forget strategy, pass him
choices.sub: Send it and take the risk

outcomes.box: You lose about 40s in the lane and come out in traffic, betting that two fast laps on new tyres are worth more than the place you just gave up.
outcomes.wait: You stay on old rubber while he gets new ones, and you need clean air plus a mistake from him to make it work.
outcomes.attack: Passing a car with the same tyres on the same fuel is the hardest thing in the sport, and running into the back of him ends both afternoons.

cards.reveal: Hamilton never stopped again from here. He finished P2, Antonelli P1.

cards.title: Hadjar spent the race in somebody's mirrors
cards.text: Close enough for DRS for long stretches and still no way through. This is what modern F1 traffic actually looks like, and it happened to 6 drivers today.

cards.title: Who has the fastest lap on the board at the flag?
cards.text: It almost always lands late, when the car is light and the track has rubber all over it, and it is worth a point to whoever finishes in the top ten.
cards.reveal: Antonelli on lap 17, 1:31.607, in a Mercedes.

cards.title: Antonelli had the quickest car underneath him
cards.text: Ranked on median clean lap, which strips out traffic, safety cars and one-off heroics. It does not always match the result.

cards.title: Perez went the other way: 4 places lost
cards.text: P18 on the grid, P22 at the flag, and 1 stops when most of the field did 1. Strategy, damage, or simply a car that would not do on Sunday what it did on Saturday. Qualifying flatters whoever can put one lap together; a race asks for sixty.

cards.title: Albon: P22 on the grid, P18 at the flag
cards.text: 4 places gained, 4 of them by passing somebody on track. This is the drive nobody will mention on Monday, because the cameras live at the front and the story of a race is written from there. The timing sheet does not care where the cameras were.

cards.title: Lawson nursed one set for 16 laps
cards.text: On the mediums, from lap 1 to lap 17. Every lap you stretch is a lap you do not lose in the pit lane, and every lap you stretch is also a set of tyres getting slower underneath you. The whole afternoon is that argument, run at 300 km/h.

cards.title: 32 yellow flag calls
cards.text: Debris, spins and cars parked where they should not be. A yellow means lift and do not overtake, so it costs real lap time to whoever happens to arrive at that corner while it is out, and nothing at all to the car half a lap ahead. Most of them were waved in the same part of the circuit, around marshalling post 3, which usually means one corner kept catching people out.

cards.title: Antonelli: 1:31.607
cards.text: The quickest anybody went all afternoon, in a Mercedes, and it came on lap 17 of 17. They almost always do: by then the fuel is nearly gone, the car is at its lightest of the day, and the track has an afternoon of rubber laid into it. A lap 1 time and a lap 50 time are barely the same sport.

cards.title: Antonelli wins it
cards.text: P1 Antonelli · P2 Hamilton · P3 Norris. After 17 laps and the best part of two hours, Hamilton crossed the line 2.745s behind. The gaps at the end of a race almost never reflect the gaps during it.

cards.title: How far behind was Hamilton at the flag?
cards.text: 17 laps, the best part of two hours of racing, and the whole thing comes down to this one number.
cards.reveal: 2.745 seconds after 17 laps. A single trip down the pit lane costs about 40s today, which is 14 times the margin this race was decided by.
